page.description: Guix System editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: The GNU project's standalone system built from the Guix package manager: the whole machine is described in one Scheme file, with transactional upgrades and rollbacks, Linux-libre and the GNU Shepherd init system.
pros: The system is declared in one configuration file and rebuilt from it.
Transactional upgrades: every generation can be rolled back at boot.
Fully free-software distribution, with reproducible builds.
Guix also installs on top of another Linux as a package manager.
cons: Scheme configuration is a real learning curve.
Only hardware with free-software drivers and firmware is supported.
No checksum file: release artifacts carry detached OpenPGP signatures instead.
The aarch64 image is experimental and UEFI-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Guix System; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the ISO to a USB stick with dd and boot it: the guided installer partitions and formats the target disk, and everything already on that disk is deleted.
